narratives.Overview:
Reduce CPU, GPU, disk I/O and memory pressure on iOS so sustained operations stop pinning performance cores, overheating the device and draining battery -- without altering any functional contract.

Six findings (F1-F6), delivered in four phases. Phase 0 is blocking: no optimisation may be marked Done before its baseline is recorded.
narratives.Constraint:
Acceptance bar is 'measurably better than baseline'; 20% is the aim, not a gate. Shortfalls are recorded in the backlog rather than dropped.

Note the metric differs per finding: F2's gain appears in thermal state and energy, NOT wall-clock. A correctly downgraded batch scan may take LONGER while consuming less. That is success, not regression.

Reference baseline (comparisons valid only against this trio plus a recorded iOS version): iPhone 16 Pro; ~1,300 videos at ~450 MB each (~585 GB); ~1,300 actor profiles with ~2 JPGs each.
narratives.Action: Phase 0 baseline + characterization -> Phase 1 F1/F2 (highest energy yield) -> Phase 2 F3/F4 (self-contained, low risk) -> Phase 3 F5/F6 (schema-backed metadata; largest and riskiest, sequenced last).
narratives.Risk:
Per personal standards: characterization tests precede refactoring, no behaviour change inside a refactor commit, and layout/energy are validated on a physical iPhone before merge. Simulator numbers are not evidence.

Every change here touches long-running or cached paths; the project's defect inventory shows this codebase's risk concentrates at DB/filesystem seams and in tasks that outlive their views.
